- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment spikes to 0.6+ (e.g., Example 2), model overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
